To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we plug $a=\frac{\pi }{3}$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(\frac{\pi }{3})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})(x-\frac{\pi }{3})+{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3})\frac{1}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}+{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{3})\frac{1}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{3} \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{3})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3})(x-\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}){(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{3}){(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={sin}^{2}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{3}) & ={sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})={(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}=\frac{3}{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})=2(-\frac{1}{2})=-1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})=-4(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=-2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ and ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{3})$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(x-\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{(-1)}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}+\frac{(-2\sqrt{3})}{6}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{3} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(x-\frac{\pi }{3})-\frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}{(x-\frac{\pi }{3})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
